variants.name: fit
variants.description: Main model. POT: the axis comes from a global hemisphere search (600 directions plus lathe_obs.fit_axis, then 2 deg and 0.7 deg local grids) minimising rim flatness plus rotational self-consistency, in mm. The rim-flatness term is the MAD over 24 sectors of the per-sector 98th-percentile height in the rim radius window. The open end is the end with no points near the axis. The profile is polar about an interior point: per (2 deg bin, 24 sectors) the median of outer-seen and inner-seen points (view direction along the polar ray), then the median over at least 6 sectors, so the handle and markers drop out. Wall t = median outer-to-inner distance, clipped to 2-6 mm. The shell is the mid-surface +-t/2, which gives a CLOSED floor (the inner floor offset by t) and follows the rounded bottom corner. The rim is capped at the median per-sector 99th-percentile height. Handle: the largest residual cluster (points more than 8 mm outside the body) reaching more than 60 mm beyond the wall. It is a flat bar from PCA plus a trimmed plane fit to top-seen points. Width = median 3-97% lateral extent. Thickness = 2 x median depth of side-seen points below the top, clipped to 3-8 mm, or a 5 mm prior. The bar runs from inside the wall to the 99.5% tip, with a semicircular tip. A hole is cut only if the top-surface occupancy has a closed gap; none was found. LID: the axis is the smallest PCA direction, flange plane refit and 3 tilt iterations. The centre comes from a circle fit to the per-sector edge. The top-surface profile is the median over sectors, two passes, with a quadratic dome under the arch. The underside is top - 2.5 mm (prior; never observed). The arch is a strap swept along the observed top curve (75th percentile of top-seen points per 3 mm bin), with width from the lateral extent and thickness from side-seen points. BOTH: markers come from compact residual clusters (at least 60 points, diagonal 6-35 mm, sphere-fit median residual under 2 mm, ball within -3..20 mm of the body or handle surface). Oversize clusters are re-split above 12 mm. The free radius is kept only if 5-9.5 mm and well supported, otherwise the 7 mm prior is used. A stem is added only if the gap holds at least 15 points and at least twice a lateral control count. All parts are unioned with manifold3d into one watertight mesh.

variants.name: nostem
variants.description: Same as fit, but markers are bare spheres with no stems. Stem evidence passed rarely, so this mesh is byte-identical to fit for 7 of 9 episode/object pairs (pot 41, 42, 43, 44, 45, 27 and the lid). It differs only for pot ep2 and ep26.

variants.name: tsdf
variants.description: The fitted lathe body (same axis and profile as fit), plus the faces of our own library_v3 TSDF mesh that lie outside the body by more than 8 mm (handle and markers). This is the earlier 'body + TSDF handle' construction (hybrid.py rule) on the new body. For the lid: library faces more than 8 mm above the fitted top surface.

variants.name: thick
variants.description: Same as fit, but the body wall or sheet thickness is doubled (pot about 2 x measured t, lid 5 mm). A sensitivity check of the registration scale and CD-O to wall thickness.

built.summary:
Family A (white_pot and white_pot_lid) passes on both objects under the pre-registered rules. Numbers against the public scans are diagnostic [D]. Selection was GT-free: lowest obs_fidelity sum over all obs_all episodes of each object.

- **white_pot:** selected candidate is ep41, variant 'fit'. CD-O is 0.342 cm against 0.437 for library_v3, ADD is 3.05 mm against 6.7, and 0 of 8 seeds flip.
- **white_pot_lid:** selected candidate is ep2, variant 'fit'. CD-O is 0.219 cm against 0.421, ADD is 5.97 mm against 8.1, and 0 of 6 seeds flip.

Method (prim_potlid.py): a thin-walled lathe body fitted to our own stereo points, plus fitted parts, unioned with manifold3d into one watertight mesh (pot about 16k faces, lid about 9k).
- **Pot:**
  - The body is a polar profile from the median over sectors of outer-seen and inner-seen points, with a constant measured wall and a closed floor offset from the observed inner floor.
  - The handle is a flat bar.
  - Marker balls are spheres with the 7 mm prior or a free radius.
- **Lid:**
  - The body is a domed sheet with a 2.5 mm underside offset from the observed top surface.
  - The handle is a swept strap along the observed arch.
  - Marker balls as for the pot.

A key fix was the pot axis. lathe_obs.fit_axis missed by 9 to 78 deg on these episodes. A global rim-flatness plus rotational-consistency search gives axes that agree within about 2.5 deg across all 8 episodes.

Across 32 pot candidates the GT-free score ranks well: Spearman 0.85 against CD-O. The diagnostic oracles are pot ep43 'tsdf' (0.309 cm / 3.1 mm) and lid ep2 'tsdf' (0.216 cm / 3.5 mm).

Negative findings:
- The fitted pot handle and markers are worse than our old TSDF appendages on the same new body (variant means 0.415 vs 0.366 cm). Most of the gain comes from the new thin lathe body and axis, not from the fitted parts.
- 'nostem' is identical to 'fit' for 7 of 9 episode/object pairs (stems almost never supported), so only 3 distinct variants were tested.
- Lid episode 0 has no usable points, so the lid rests on ep2 alone.
- No handle hole was supported by evidence.
- Some marker spheres are spurious.

39 meshes were scored against scans in total (36 final candidates, 2 dev bug-checks, 1 library reference). Nothing was committed.

audit.gt_leak_evidence:

- the obs npz (load_obs reads only 'pts' and 'cam');
- --lib, used only by variant tsdf, which is meshes/library_v3/<obj>.glb. recon_mesh.py builds that mesh from our stereo along our own tracked poses.
- --axis_cache, which holds only our own fitted centre and axis.

Nothing reads loc/t3/mesh, *_align.npz, mocap or parquet poses. The drivers do not either: run_fit.sh passes only obs_all npz plus the library glb, and select.py calls only obs_fidelity.py. I grepped the 14 dev/explore/dbg/axis_test scripts. They load only obs npz or the fit json, never scans.

variants.name: occ
variants.description: Slab between the two fitted face planes. Thickness is the two-face separation, or the family median of 8.8 mm when only one face was seen. Outline is the 2-D occupancy of slab points (cells with >= 1 point, 1.5 mm grid), closed 3 mm, holes filled, opened 4.5 mm, smoothed contour. A slot is carved when the voxel hit grid shows the other board passing through the slab on one half only. Marker spheres come from centre voting and a robust LSQ fit with a 7 mm radius prior (sigma 1.5 mm), accepted if seen in >= 10 frames, r 4-11 mm, RMS <= 1.6 mm and touching the outline. Stems are added only if points support them; none were. Union by manifold3d, watertight, about 1.3k-4.5k faces.

variants.name: occ_d2
variants.description: Same as occ, but outline cells need >= 2 points. This gives a tighter outline with less track-jitter halo and fewer stray points.

variants.name: rect
variants.description: Minimum-area rectangle of the outline body (an 8 mm opening removes tabs and spurs; all significant components are used), minus the slot, plus markers. It fills in unseen corners and edges.

variants.name: occ_nm
variants.description: occ without marker spheres. Ablation to measure what the markers do for registration.

CD-O 0.189 is within the 0.192 limit and ADD 3.3 within the 3.4 limit, but extra seed 44 registers rotated 179.6 deg about the board normal, so flips are 1/6 (add_all 31 mm). The selected candidate is also the oracle by CD-O; ep24 occ gives 0.190 / 3.1 with 1/6 flips (seed 22). Every ep24 variant flips 1/6 (occ_nm: 0.192 / 2.5 / 1/6), so markers did not reduce flips for this board. ep24 fit: both faces seen, thickness 6.2 mm, 4 marker spheres (r 6.7-8.2 mm), no slot found. One sphere at u = -125 mm sits on an outline tab that may be a finger: ep24 has no hand filtering because hands.npz returned 404. One-board check: the ep23 points under this label are not one whole board. They are a partial board (about half the width, one face, two separate patches; frac_far 0.016) whose candidates register about 77 mm from the scan pose with 5-6/6 flips (CD-O 0.42-0.79), and against ep24's points obs_to_mesh is 60 mm. So the ep23 wooden_piece_1 track is broken or offset; GT-free selection rejected it.

FAIL on all three tests. CD-O 0.229 against a 0.186 limit, ADD 78.7 mm, 3/6 flips (the eval seed included). The flip axes are the long axis (face swap) and the normal (in-plane turn). Even unflipped seeds have an 8 mm anchor offset. GT-free selection chose ep23, where both faces were seen and the thickness came out at 11.4 mm (fid 1.968). It passed over ep24, where only one face was seen and the family-median thickness of 8.8 mm was used (fid 2.170), yet ep24 scores far better [D]: the oracle ep24 occ gets CD-O 0.164 / ADD 4.1, still with 1/6 flips (seed 55); ep24 occ_d2 gets 0.165 / 3.8 / 1/6. So the observed two-face thickness hurts CD-O, and obs_fidelity cannot see this because the points support it. Markers reduce flips here: ep24 goes from 4/6 (occ_nm) to 1/6 (occ), and ep23 from 4/6 to 3/6 (occ_d2). Slot: half-resolution stereo bridges it when the board lies flat, so it was found only in the voxel hit grid of assembled frames. ep23 puts it on the v+ half at u 0.0 (6.2 mm wide); ep24 puts it on the v- half at u +13 mm, in the same object frame. That disagreement points to a label swap, a track flip in one episode, or a detector error. One-board check: ep23 and ep24 each look like one board, but the ep24 outline is skewed (258 mm long) by track drift.

problems: Neither board passes. All 16 candidates have at least 1/6 registration flips; the library_v3 TSDF meshes have 0/6. Flip axes [D, flip-axis check]: 180 deg about the board normal, which our corner-marker layout barely distinguishes, and 180 deg about the long axis (face swap). Flipped and unflipped seeds have almost the same CD-O, so our asymmetric features (markers, slot, outline tabs) are too weak to decide the kit's start selection.

The GT-free selection is misled by thickness for wooden_piece_2. The stereo two-face separation is 11.4 mm for board 2 (ep23; face- seen only at grazing angles, |cos| about 0.25) and 6.2 mm for board 1 (ep24). The one-face ep24 board 2 with the family-median 8.8 mm scored CD-O 0.164 against 0.229 for the selected ep23 [D]. Hypothesis: the two-face separation is biased by track or grazing-view errors. The test that would falsify it: compare face offsets measured only from frontal views (|cos| > 0.7) of both faces in one episode.

The ep23 wooden_piece_1 label is not a usable whole board. Its points cover about half the width, one face only, in two separate patches; it sits about 77 mm from the scan pose and 60 mm from ep24's points. This is likely the track failure or identity problem known for ep23. The episode is effectively lost for board 1.

The slot is invisible in our depth when the board lies flat, because half-resolution stereo bridges a 6-9 mm gap above a table about 9 mm below. The only evidence is the obs_points voxel hit grid in assembled frames. For board 2 the detected slot side disagrees between ep23 (v+) and ep24 (v-) in the same object frame, which suggests a label swap or track flip in one episode. No slot was found for board 1. The slot width comes from the other board's crossing points: 6.2 mm, one-sided and unreliable.
ep24 has no hand filtering: hands.npz was 404 in prep_obs. Hand blobs remain; most are rejected as markers, but one accepted wp1 sphere sits on an outline tab that may be a finger.

Scan use, counted: 18 distinct meshes scored with mesh_metric (16 candidates = 4 variants x 2 episodes x 2 objects, plus the 2 library_v3 baselines as a harness check, which reproduced 0.222/2.4 and 0.216/3.6). As bug-hunting diagnostics on meshes among those 18, I also ran cdo_decomp on 3 (both selected, plus library wp2) and a flip-axis registration check on 2. These found no bug: spheres sit at the fitted centres and the scale ratio is about 1. No parameter was changed after scan scoring; the code sha1 was recorded before the final run.

The 'markers' column in candidates.jsonl reports the fit's marker count even for occ_nm, whose mesh has no markers (the table above corrects this). Stems were never detected: the fitted ball centres lie at or just inside the face plane, with caps about 7-10 mm above it.

Neither board passes the pre-registered test; this is a clean negative result. prim_boards.py fits a two-plane slab with an occupancy outline (smoothed contour) to our obs_all points, adds a slot taken from the voxel hit grid and marker spheres (centre voting plus LSQ with a 7 mm prior), and unions them into a watertight mesh. I built 16 candidates (2 boards x episodes 23 and 24 x 4 variants) and selected per object by obs_fidelity against both episodes' points.

- wooden_piece_1: selected ep24 occ_d2, CD-O 0.189 (library 0.222) and ADD 3.3 mm (library 2.4). Both are within the limits, but 1 of 6 seeds flips, so it fails. It is also the scan oracle.
- wooden_piece_2: selected ep23 occ_d2, CD-O 0.229, ADD 78.7 mm and 3/6 flips, so it fails on every test. The oracle, ep24 occ, reaches CD-O 0.164 and ADD 4.1 mm but still flips on 1/6 seeds. It loses the GT-free selection because the ep23 two-face thickness of 11.4 mm fits the observed points better than the 8.8 mm family median used in ep24.

Every candidate flips at least once; the library meshes never do. The flips are 180-degree turns about the board normal or about the long axis, which markers, slot and tabs do not separate strongly enough. Markers helped board 2 (ep24: 4/6 flips without them, 1/6 with) but not board 1.

The data have problems:
- The ep23 board 1 label is a broken partial board.
- The slot is invisible in the stereo depth, and its side disagrees between episodes for board 2.
- ep24 has no hand filter.

I scored 18 meshes against a scan and used all 4 variants. Nothing was committed or pushed.

audit.gt_leak_evidence: prim_boards.py (sha1 2643471f…, the same as code_sha1.txt) reads only the obs_points npz files. It uses the keys pts, cam, frame, hits, lo and vox. Its one import is lathe_obs.normals, which does kNN PCA normals on the points. It shells out to obs_fidelity.py (sha1 53d90e5d), which reads only the obs npz and the candidate GLBs. Neither file has a path to loc/t3/mesh, *_align.npz, mocap or parquet. I re-ran `prim_boards.py run --obs_dir obs_all` into audit_boards/rebuild: all 16 meshes came out with identical vertices and faces, and the selection was the same. So the published meshes come from the frozen code with no hand edits. The constants are round, shared by both boards and both episodes, and there is no per-object branch. None of the scan dimensions appear in the code (227 x 139 mm outline; thickness 7.25 mm for wp1 and 9.25 mm for wp2). One near-match: the marker radius prior R0 = 7 mm is close to the scan ball radii, which I measured at 6.65-7.02 mm. Its provenance is documented, though: the work log of 2026-10-13 has '7.2 mm spheres' from our own stereo, and prim_potlid uses the same prior, so I do not count it as a leak. The dev scripts written before the freeze (04:08-04:37) read only obs npz. flipaxis.py (04:53) loads the scan through mesh_metric.reference, but it was written after scoring started and is a declared diagnostic. Only one scores.jsonl in the scratchpad holds board scorings (18 lines), so the claim that nothing was scan-scored before the freeze holds. Not audited: the upstream frame provenance of the sweep tracks and the library_v3 ROI/others meshes that obs_points uses.
audit.selection_evidence: I re-ran obs_fidelity.py for each object on all 8 candidates against ep23+ep24 points (audit_boards/fid_wooden_piece_{1,2}.jsonl). Every value matched the builder's to 3 decimals. wp1 sums: ep23 occ 61.701, ep23 occ_d2 62.537, ep23 rect 8.727, ep23 occ_nm 61.701, ep24 occ 1.847, ep24 occ_d2 1.835 (min), ep24 rect 2.319, ep24 occ_nm 1.856. wp2 sums: ep23 occ 2.003, ep23 occ_d2 1.968 (min), ep23 rect 2.216, ep23 occ_nm 2.047, ep24 occ 2.207, ep24 occ_d2 2.170, ep24 rect 2.713, ep24 occ_nm 2.207. Both selections are the per-object minimum, and the independent rebuild gives the same selection. Two caveats on what this metric can see. (a) For wp1, ep23 contributes only 44.5k of 2.09M points (2 %), so the 90 % trim drops it: the wp1 choice is effectively ep24-only. (b) A fit where only one face was seen is penalised by its unseen face. ep24 wp2 occ against its own points has mesh_to_obs 3.24 mm, so the metric favours episodes where both faces were seen, whatever their identity or orientation.
audit.shape_check:
I viewed both selected renders, the wp2 oracle render and the two ep23 board crops, and projected each mesh against the scan in the shared frame (audit_boards/scan_vs_cand_yz.png, diagnostic). The pot, lid and rack crops belong to other families and were not relevant. The crops show a flat wooden board about 227 x 139 mm, with a slot from one long edge to mid-width, notched corners, and dark ball markers on stems.

wooden_piece_1, ep24_occ_d2: a flat slab of the right size, about 6.2 mm thick (scan 7.25). Its two +x spheres at the z+ end match the scan markers within about 4 mm. It is missing things: there is no slot (the crop and the scan both have one at z≈0 from the y+ edge) and no corner notches. It also has spurious parts: a blob of about 15-20 mm beyond the z- end (the mesh reaches z = -131.8 mm against the scan's -112.4), a tab on the y- edge, and 2 of its 4 spheres on the wrong face (-x) at the z- end, where the scan has +x markers. So it reads as 'a board' but not this board's details.

wooden_piece_2, ep23_occ_d2: it looks like a slotted board with corner balls, which superficially resembles the crop. Against the wp2 scan, though, its features are on the wrong side. Its 4 ball bumps are on +x while the wp2 scan's 3 markers are on -x, and its slot is on the y- half while the scan's slot (and ep24's own wp2 fit) is on the y+ half. Its marker layout and slot side match board 1 rotated 180° about the board normal: all 4 markers within 6-12 mm, and the slot side matches. The ep24 oracle has the slot and its one marker on the correct sides.

Every fitted ball centre sits at the face plane. On the scans the ball centres are about 10 mm above the face, on stems. So all markers are modelled about 10 mm too low.
issues: Reproduced exactly: cdo_eval, add_eval and flips_all for both selected meshes, the wp2 oracle and both library_v3 baselines match the builder to the last digit (audit_boards/rescore.jsonl). Pass-rule arithmetic: wp1 meets CD-O (0.1893 <= 0.192) and ADD (3.31 <= 3.4) but has flips_all = 1 (seed 44, 179.6 deg), so it FAILS. wp2 fails all three tests (0.2291 > 0.186; 78.69 > 4.6 mm; 3 flips including the eval seed). Both FAIL verdicts are correct.

wp1 meets the CD-O limit only narrowly. The margin is 0.0027 cm, while the per-seed CD-O sd is 0.0048; seed 55 gives 0.1992, over the 0.192 limit. The CD-O pass holds at the eval seed, not robustly. In the flipped seed 44, CD-O (0.1851) is lower than in most unflipped seeds, so the mesh carries almost no usable asymmetry.

The builder's main diagnosis for wp2 is not established. The builder blames the two-face thickness (11.4 vs 8.8 mm). But the ep23 'wooden_piece_2' fit has its marker bumps on +x and its slot on the y- half. Both are opposite to ep24's own wp2 fit, which is a GT-free signal, and opposite to the wp2 scan, which is diagnostic. They match board 1 turned 180 deg about the normal. The work log already records a frame-0 board identity swap in ep23 and a 'swapped + 180 deg about x' identity fix for eval 25. More likely explanation: identity swap plus flip of the ep23 track. Thickness is confounded with it (wp2 scan 9.25 mm, ep23 fit 11.4). The test that would falsify the swap explanation: refit ep23 wp2 with t forced to 8.8 mm. If CD-O stays near 0.23, thickness was not the cause.

The builder stated the slot-side disagreement but not the marker-face disagreement (ep23 wp2 +x against ep24 wp2 -x). Both were visible without GT, and selection took the episode whose layout contradicts the other. The pre-registered rule has no identity or consistency check, so selection followed the rule; the outcome is still likely wrong for wp2.

wp1 ep24 has 2 spurious markers, not 1. Both -x spheres at the z- end, (-12.4,-107.9) and (15.4,-125.2) mm, are on the wrong face: the scan has only +x markers. They are probably hands, since ep24 has no hands.npz (confirmed: data/sweep/ep24 holds only poses.npz). The outline also has a spurious tab and a blob. The mesh runs about 19 mm beyond the scan's z- end, and its thickness is 6.2 mm against the scan's 7.25.

Systematic marker error: every fitted ball centre lies at the face plane (h_face -3.6 to +3.8 mm). The scan balls (r 6.65-7.02 mm) are centred about 10 mm above the face on stems, so all markers are about 10 mm too low. Some ep23 wp2 radii (9.5-10.9 mm) are near the 11 mm acceptance cap; these may not be real balls.
t_default = 8.8 mm is the median of only two values, 6.22 and 11.38. The 11.38 likely comes from a misidentified or flipped track, so the family default rests on one questionable measurement.

Minor: the occ variant is described as 'about 1.3k-4.5k faces', but variants range from 12 faces (ep23 wp1 rect) to 4552. The markers column in candidates.jsonl is wrong for occ_nm, as the builder already said.

Scan-use count: confirmed 18 scored meshes in the builder's run and no other board scorings in the scratchpad. My audit added 5 rescorings, all repeats of meshes already scored, and read the wp1/wp2 scans for diagnostic geometry: marker balls, faces, slot side and extents. All audit files are in prim/audit_boards/. Nothing was committed.
audit.verdict: The builder's numbers reproduce exactly and both FAIL verdicts are correct. Selection followed the pre-registered rule, and I found no ground-truth leak in fitting: the frozen script rebuilds all 16 meshes identically and reads only our obs points. The interpretation is weaker than the claims. wp1 meets the CD-O limit only narrowly (within seed noise), and 2 of its 4 markers are spurious, not 1. For wp2, the selected ep23 mesh most likely comes from a swapped or flipped track: its marker face and slot side are opposite to both ep24's fit and the wp2 scan, and they match board 1 turned 180° about the normal. So the thickness explanation is unproven and confounded. A clean negative result for this family, but its stated cause for wp2 should be revised.

Our stereo points on this white rack carry view-dependent biases of several mm, so leans and wall profiles are set by priors rather than fitted. Markers: only the front-wall and right-end balls are reliably found.

audit.gt_leak_evidence:
No direct ground-truth read. I read prim_rack.py (sha1 ca2aea0d on disk, matching the builder's claim) in full, plus the helpers it imports or calls: lathe_obs.normals, prim_potlid (markers_from, fit_sphere, mf_sphere/mf_cylinder, from_mf) and obs_fidelity.py (via subprocess). The only file inputs are the obs_all/*.npz arrays pts/cam/frame/args. Nothing touches loc/t3/mesh, *_align.npz, mocap or parquet. The obs_all npz were made upstream by obs_points.py from our own sweep poses (data/sweep/epNN/poses.npz) and stereo depth; library_v3 is used there only as an ROI box.

Two scan-informed choices exist, and the builder disclosed both:
(1) T_WALL = 0.0025 is a per-object constant equal to the scan-measured rack wall median in docs/research/mesh-2026-10-26/README.md ("rack | 2.5 mm", tagged [D], from scripts/scan_stats.py). The code comment says only "task brief: thin moulded shells", which hides that the figure comes from the scan. It sets the floor plate and the cup-holder wall, and it is part of why the floor top lands within about 0.2 mm of the scan (ep31: ours -5.5, scan median -5.6; ep12: ours -8.0, scan -8.2).
(2) CUP_LEAN=False and the new cup_upright estimator came after the scan was seen. Timeline: dev1 scan scores written 05:51:41, then prim_rack/dev/diag_regions.py ([D], modified 05:53:14) printed the scan's cup-holder x/y extents at four heights and the floor height along x, then prim_rack .pyc rebuilt 05:55, the first upright-cup builds at 05:57-05:58, and final at 06:03.

In ep31 its back face is about 10 mm short (y 56.5 against 66-68) and its top is about 9 mm high (109.6 against about 101 mm). The cup corner radius varies by episode (18/20/22/26/20/20 mm). audit.verdict:
PASS confirmed [D], with caveats. I re-scored the selected joint_joint.glb at CD-O 0.4535 cm (limit 0.525), ADD 6.414 mm (limit 7.0) and 0/7 flips, identical to the builder's numbers. Its obs_fidelity of 6.116 is the lowest of the 12 final candidates.

The fitting code reads no ground truth. Two choices are still scan-informed, and both were disclosed: T_WALL = 2.5 mm is the scan's measured rack wall median, and the upright cup holder was adopted after a scan diagnostic that also printed the cup extents. The final cup does not match those extents, so I found no sign that scan dimensions were copied.

The pass is narrow on ADD. The margin is 0.59 mm, ADD is 0.4 mm worse than the library, and one extra seed reaches 7.7 mm. Superseded builds on disk have lower fidelity. One of them, final_v0's joint, was dropped by a marker rule added by hand afterwards; scored for this audit only [D], it also passes (0.463 / 5.88). So the post-hoc rule did not decide the verdict.

The mesh looks like the rack: tray, cup holder and 2 x 6 pegs. It lacks the right-end ribs and the marker stems, and its cup holder is a straight box rather than the real rounded shape.
